title: Microburst credit fragmentation causing sustained reserved-pool shortfall for multi-tenant workloads
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Summary: During a series of weekday traffic spikes (2025-02-13 -> 2025-02-14) multiple mid-size customers using Dedicated reserved pools experienced sustained token starvation and elevated tail latency. Unlike prior burst-credit depletion incidents, this event was driven by fragmentation in the microburst accounting ledger that prevented partial burst credits from being reclaimed and recomposed for new short bursts. The autoscaler did not trigger timely top-up because the headroom signal was underestimated.

Why this ticket: This is the triage and permanent fix ticket: investigate root cause, land a correctness patch in the burst-credit reconciler, add targeted telemetry and alerting, ship a safe rollout, and coordinate customer communications and postmortem items.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create two tenants A and B sharing a reserved pool with burst credits enabled.
2) Issue a sequence of staggered 50ms microbursts to tenant A (20 bursts / minute) interleaved with 10 larger bursts to tenant B.
3) Observe burst-credit ledger entries: many sub-token allocations remain fragmented (less than microburstMinimum) and are not coalesced.
4) Simulate autoscaler horizon evaluation at t+30s and t+120s; headroom projection underestimates required top-up and scaleup is not scheduled.

Reproducible locally using the autoscaler-sim harness and the reserved-pool-allocator binary with flags: --microburst-min=64 --reconcile-window=15s
investigation_notes:
- Initial alert raised by SRE (oncall) and escalated by Customer Success for 3 tenants.
- Correlated with recent optimization (PR #8421) that changed ledger bucketization to reduce GC cost; regression introduced a case where sub-token fragments were marked as "soft-orphan" and skipped during reconcile.
- Ledger snapshot analysis showed ~18% of burst credits were in 1-3 token fragments across pool members; these fragments were below microburstMinimum threshold and not being compacted.
- Autoscaler headroom heuristic relies on aggregated free_tokens metric which was artificially low due to accounting fragmentation.
- Root cause: combination of (a) bucketization change + (b) reconcile pass short-circuit when pool load > 75% leading to missed compaction opportunities.
proposed_fix:
1) Rework reconciler to always attempt a lightweight compaction pass that coalesces fragments at the start of each reconcile window, bounded by CPU budget.
2) Adjust bucketization to keep one rolling compaction slot per tenant so tiny fragments are reclaimed within two reconcile cycles.
3) Add a safety override: if free_tokens < threshold_for_pool AND observed_microburst_rate > X, schedule speculative top-up even if aggregated headroom looks sufficient.
4) Add unit and integration tests for ledger fragmentation scenarios.
5) Telemetry: emit metrics burst_ledger_fragment_ratio, compaction_passs_duration, speculative_topup_trigger_count.
testing_summary:
- Local sim harness recreates fragmentation and shows compaction reduces fragmented tokens from ~18% to <1% within 90s.
- Staging run across two regions for 48h with synthetic multi-tenant load: no observable regression in latency, CPU overhead <3%.
- End-to-end soak with a copy of affected customers' traffic pattern for 6h: no bursts starved, autoscaler top-ups occurred correctly.
- Added regression unit tests and snapshot tests for ledger state transitions.
rollout_plan:
- Canary: deploy allocator v2.12.3 to 5% of Dedicated pools (low-traffic region) with speculative-topup disabled by default flags. Monitor burst_ledger_fragment_ratio and avail_tokens metrics for 24h.
- Enable speculative-topup in canary for another 12h if no regressions.
- Gradual ramp to 50% over 48h, then to 100% over next 24h.
- If increased CPU or unexpected scaleups observed, rollback to v2.12.2 and revert flags.
- Post-deploy: run reconciliation verification job across all reserved pools to ensure fragment ratio below 2%.
customer_communications:
- Immediate: CS team notified affected customers on 2025-02-14 with mitigation guidance (increase temporary reserved pool burst_limit, enable fallback to hosted plan).
- Post-fix: Coordinated message sent on 2025-02-19 summarizing root cause and steps taken; offered 10% invoice credit for affected hour window.
- Follow-up: Scheduled 1:1 sync with top-3 affected customers to review incident telemetry and roadmap changes.
monitoring_and_alerting:
- New alerts: burst_ledger_fragment_ratio > 10% for > 5m; speculative_topup_trigger_count > 0 and pool_free_tokens < critical_threshold.
- Dashboards added: Reserved Pool Health (fragment ratio, avg_free_tokens, reconcile_latency) cloned into console and shared with SRE and CS.
- Actionable runbook update: if fragment_ratio rises >8% escalate to allocator-oncall and flip compaction_override flag.
resolution: Patch merged and rolled out as allocator v2.12.3. Fragmentation metric decreased from median 12% -> 0.8% across affected pools. Autoscaler headroom projections recovered and speculative top-ups prevented further token starvation. No further customer escalations after rollout.
